newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan semiconductor production value seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan semiconductor production value seen rising.

text.p: The production value of Taiwan's red-hot semiconductor industry will rise to T$228.6 billion (US$8.3 billion) in 1997 from T$175.6 billion in 1996, Taiwan's top economic policy-making body said on Tuesday.

A research report by the Council for Economic Planning and Development predicted the semiconductor sector, an export juggernaut, would post a production value of T$460.5 billion in 2000 and T$1.175 trillion in 2005.

"Our report predicts continuing growth for the industry because Taiwan has a huge domestic computer market, good production line flexibility and strong research know-how," a council official said by telephone.
Most of Taiwan's chipmakers have been benefactors of the island's surging computer market, reporting sound profits in 1996 despite a global plunge in chip prices.
The island's biggest chipmaker, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, posted a net profit of T$39.4 billion in 1996 compared to T$28.77 billion in 1995.

Latest government data show Taiwan's computer industry grew an average 28 percent a year from 1992 to 1995, hitting a production value of US$19.7 billion in 1995 to rank as the world's third largest after the United States and Japan. ($ = T$27.57)
